title: Pythagoras' theorem for the hypotenuse

draft.title: Pythagoras' theorem: hypotenuse
card: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle. It is opposite the right angle.
Pythagoras' theorem says c² = a² + b², where c is the hypotenuse and a and b are the other two sides.
To find the hypotenuse, square both short sides, add the results, then take the square root.
Example: the short sides are 6 and 8. c² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. So c = √100 = 10.
draft.remember: Square the two short sides, add them, then take the square root.

a.q: A right-angled triangle has short sides of 5 cm and 12 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
a.why: c² = 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169, and √169 = 13. Choosing 17 adds the sides without squaring them. Choosing 169 forgets the square root.
a.clue: Square each short side, add, then take the root.

b.q: A ramp rises 9 m up a wall and the ground below it is 12 m long. The wall meets the ground at a right angle. How long is the ramp's sloping surface?
b.why: The slope is the hypotenuse: c² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, and √225 = 15. Choosing 21 adds 9 and 12 without squaring. Choosing 225 stops before the square root.
b.clue: The sloping side is opposite the right angle.
